The lineup can change weekly. Check the Vancouver Farmers Markets (VFM) website or social media on Tuesday evenings to see exactly which farms and distillers will be attending.

places.name: False Creek Farmers Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/tomato-gm2220809697-637211815

The False Creek Farmers Market offers one of the most scenic shopping backdrops in the city. Set along the seawall near Science World, this market captures the relaxed, waterfront energy of Vancouver. It serves as a vital community gathering spot for residents of Olympic Village, Mount Pleasant, and the False Creek flats, blending fresh local food with beautiful views of the marina and downtown skyline.
What to Expect
Waterside Atmosphere: Shop while enjoying the breeze off the water. The market's linear layout along the seawall makes for a pleasant, stroll-through shopping experience.
Organic and Sustainable Focus: You will find a high concentration of organic growers and small-scale family farms bringing everything from vine-ripened tomatoes to fresh herbs and stone fruits.
Craft Beverages: This market is a great place to discover local craft breweries, cideries, and distilleries offering tastings and bottles to go.
Community Connection: With a playground nearby and plenty of green space at Concord Community Park, it’s a high-energy, family-friendly environment where neighbors often stop to chat.
Key Information
Location: Concord Community Park (88 Pacific Boulevard), located between Science World and the Cambie Street Bridge.
Season: Typically runs from early June through early October.
Hours: Thursdays, 3:00 PM – 7:00 PM.

Access: Ideally located for those on foot or bike via the Seawall. It is a 5-minute walk from the Main Street-Science World SkyTrain station and accessible via the Aquabus or False Creek Ferries at the Terry Fox Plaza dock.
Payment: Most vendors are equipped for tap payments; however, the Market Money program is available at the info booth if you need to trade card payments for market tokens.
Tips
Since it's located directly on a major bike path, many shoppers arrive on two wheels. Ensure you have panniers or a secure front basket for your produce.
This market peaks between 5:00 PM and 6:00 PM as commuters head home. If you prefer a quieter experience, try to arrive right at opening or during the final hour.
Pick up some artisanal cheese, fresh bread, and fruit, then head to the nearby grassy areas or the seawall benches to enjoy a sunset picnic by the water.
Since the market stays open until 7:00 PM, the late-season summer light over the water is spectacular—perfect for capturing photos of your market haul with the city in the background.

places.name: Kitsilano Farmers’ Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/shoppers-explore-a-local-farmers-market-in-vancouver-gm458469913-27138515

The Kitsilano Farmers’ Market is a staple of the West Side summer lifestyle. Located in the parking lot of the Kitsilano Community Centre, this market is famous for its festive, neighborhood-block-party vibe. It is one of the city’s largest and most popular markets, drawing crowds of locals who stop by after a morning at the beach or a workout at the nearby park.
What to Expect
Vibrant Community Hub: With live acoustic music usually playing and plenty of families and dogs in tow, this market feels like a true community celebration.
Massive Selection: Because of its size, you’ll find an extensive array of vendors—ranging from large-scale organic vegetable farms and orchards to specialized micro-producers.
High-Quality Meat and Seafood: This is an excellent location to source locally raised meats, sustainable seafood, and specialty items like pasture-raised eggs and grass-fed dairy.

Prepared Food Paradise: The market is known for its excellent selection of food trucks and prepared food vendors. You’ll find everything from authentic tamales and wood-fired pizza to gourmet coffee and vegan treats.
Key Information
Location: Kitsilano Community Centre (2690 Larch Street), at the corner of Larch Street and 10th Avenue.
Season: Typically runs from early May through late October.
Hours: Sundays, 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM.

Access: The market is easily reached via the #9 or #99 B-Line buses along Broadway. For those driving, street parking is available in the surrounding residential area, but it can be challenging to find a spot.
Payment: Most vendors accept card payments, but the info booth can also provide "Market Money" tokens in exchange for debit/credit if needed.
Tips
This market is exceptionally busy. The most popular fruit vendors and bakeries often have lineups within the first 30 minutes, and star items can sell out by noon.
The market is adjacent to Connaught Park, which has plenty of green space, a playground, and benches. It’s the perfect place to enjoy your market snacks immediately.
Given the variety of goods—from heavy root vegetables to delicate berries and artisanal breads—you’ll likely end up buying more than you planned. A wagon or a large backpack is a smart move here.

While the market is outdoors and very pet-friendly, it can get very crowded. If your dog is nervous in tight spaces, it might be easier to navigate during the final hour of the market when the crowds thin out.

places.name: Kitsilano Winter Farmers Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/close-up-and-textures-of-freshly-harvested-organic-okanagan-transparent-apple-at-gm2166549057-586648341

The winter iteration of the Kitsilano market provides a vital connection to local food during the cooler months. While the summer market takes place at the community center, the winter version moves to the nearby high school parking lot, maintaining the neighborhood's commitment to seasonal eating year-round. It offers a slightly more intimate feel while still delivering a robust selection of cold-weather essentials.
What to Expect

Winter Harvest Specialties: This is the place to find an abundance of hardy root vegetables, squash, kale, and greenhouse-grown greens. You'll also find a steady supply of storage crops like apples and pears from the Okanagan.

Cozy Prepared Foods: Vendors pivot to offer warmer fare, including hot coffee, hearty soups, and fresh-baked breads. It is a popular spot to grab a warm snack while browsing the stalls in the crisp morning air.
Fermented and Preserved Goods: Since fresh fruit is less varied in winter, the market shines with artisanal preserves, pickles, sauerkraut, and kombucha.
Holiday Gifting: During the late autumn and early winter, there is an increased presence of local crafters and makers offering handmade jewelry, textiles, and woodcrafts.
https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/close-up-and-textures-of-freshly-harvested-organic-okanagan-beans-and-peas-at-trout-gm2166548911-586648302
Key Information
Location: Kitsilano Secondary School Parking Lot (2706 Trafalgar Street), at the corner of 10th Avenue and Trafalgar.
Season: Typically runs from early November through late April.
Hours: Sundays, 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM.
Access: The market is well-served by the #9 and #99 B-Line buses along Broadway. Bike racks are available nearby, and street parking can be found in the surrounding residential blocks.
Payment: Most vendors accept card payments, and the market information booth is available for the "Market Money" program.
Tips
As the market is held in an open-air parking lot, it can feel quite chilly, especially if there is a breeze off the water. Dress in layers to stay comfortable while you shop.
This is an excellent time to buy in bulk for items like potatoes, onions, and carrots, which stay fresh for a long time in cool storage.
Some specialty vendors only attend every other week during the winter. It’s worth checking the vendor map online to ensure your favorites are there before you head out.
Take the time to talk to the producers. Winter is a great season to learn about the preservation techniques they use to keep local food on the table during the off-season.

places.name: Mount Pleasant Farmers’ Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/shoppers-explore-a-local-farmers-market-in-vancouver-gm458470765-27138571

The Mount Pleasant Farmers’ Market is one of Vancouver’s newest and most community-focused markets, located on the suburban edge of the vibrant Mount Pleasant neighborhood. Set right next to the famous Dude Chilling Park, this market has a relaxed, grass-roots feel that captures the artistic and family-friendly spirit of the area.
What to Expect
Community Vibe: This market feels like a backyard gathering. It’s smaller and more intimate than the Kitsilano or Trout Lake markets, making it easy to navigate and chat with the local producers.
Picnic-Ready Provisions: Many shoppers pick up fresh berries, artisanal cheeses, and baked goods to immediately enjoy on the grass at the adjacent park.

Curated Artisan Selection: You’ll find about 35 vendors each week, featuring a carefully selected mix of organic produce, ethically raised meats, and small-batch pantry staples like pickles and preserves.
Local Brews and Spirits: The market frequently hosts local craft breweries and distillers, offering a great way to sample and buy regional beers and spirits.
Key Information
Location: 8th Avenue and Guelph Street, at the edge of Dude Chilling Park (2300 Guelph Street).
Season: The 2026 summer season runs from May 3 to November 1.
Hours: Sundays, 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM.
Access: Easily reachable by bike or transit. It’s a short walk from the major bus routes on Broadway, Main Street, and Kingsway.
Payment: Vendors typically accept card and mobile payments, with the "Market Money" program available at the information booth for those needing tokens.
Tips
Since the market is right at the park, it’s a popular spot for a playground date. Bring a picnic blanket and enjoy the live music often found at the market while your kids play nearby.
Because it’s a smaller market, limited-supply items like heirloom tomatoes or specialty stone fruits can go fast. Aim to arrive within the first hour for the best selection.
The area is very bike-friendly, with plenty of places to lock up your bike along the park perimeter.
The lineup changes slightly each week. Check the Vancouver Farmers Markets website on Saturdays to see if your favorite farm or food truck will be in attendance.

places.name: Riley Park Farmers’ Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/garlic-braids-in-a-market-stall-in-trout-lake-farmers-market-gm2165608978-585792917

The Riley Park Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the Vancouver local food scene, known for being one of the few locations that operates year-round. Located near the edge of Queen Elizabeth Park, this market provides a consistent bridge between urban residents and regional producers, offering a bustling, high-energy shopping environment every weekend.
What to Expect
Year-Round Consistency: Unlike seasonal neighborhood stops, this market transitions seamlessly between the summer harvest and the winter bounty, moving its configuration to accommodate the weather.
Vast Product Variety: Shoppers can find everything from high-altitude orchard fruits and coastal vegetables to pasture-raised meats, sustainable seafood, and specialty dairy products.
Artisan and Prepared Foods: The market is a favorite for discovering small-batch producers of kombucha, craft spirits, fermented foods, and handmade pastries.
A Social Hub: Given its proximity to local parks and the Nat Bailey Stadium, it serves as a major social meeting point for the Riley Park-Little Mountain community.
Key Information
Location: Riley Park Plaza (50 East 30th Avenue and Ontario Street), adjacent to the Hillcrest Memorial Centre.
Season: Operates year-round.
Hours: Saturdays, 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM.
Access: The market is well-served by transit, including the #3 bus on Main Street and the #15 on Cambie Street. It is also a short walk from the King Edward SkyTrain station.
Payment: Vendors are generally equipped for credit and debit tap payments, and the information booth manages the Market Money token system.
Tips

Because this is a year-round destination, it attracts a loyal following. Arriving at the 10:00 AM opening ensures the freshest selection of limited-run items like artisanal sourdough or seasonal flowers.
The market’s location makes it easy to pair your grocery shopping with a walk through Queen Elizabeth Park or a visit to the Bloedel Conservatory.
Many vendors encourage sustainability by offering discounts or simply appreciating it when you bring your own egg cartons, berry baskets, or bulk bags.
During the Winter Market months (November–April), the layout may shift slightly to utilize the paved areas of the plaza more effectively for drainage and accessibility.

places.name: Trout Lake Farmers’ Market (East Vancouver)
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/shoppers-explore-trout-lake-farmers-market-vancouver-british-columbia-canada-gm547140546-98809171

The Trout Lake Farmers Market is the birthplace of the modern farmers market movement in Vancouver and remains its most iconic location. Nestled on the north end of John Hendry Park (Trout Lake Park), this market offers a sprawling, park-like setting that draws huge crowds from across East Vancouver. It is the gold standard for those seeking a vast selection of local produce, artisanal crafts, and a true festival atmosphere.
What to Expect

Agricultural Variety: As one of the largest markets in the city, it hosts a massive array of vendors. You’ll find everything from specialty mushroom foragers and organic orchardists to heirloom tomato specialists and local flower farmers.

Park-Side Setting: The market is situated right next to the lake and forest paths. It’s common for shoppers to grab lunch from a food truck and have a picnic on the grass or take a lap around the lake after finishing their grocery run.
Artisanal Hub: Beyond the vegetables, this market is a major outlet for local potters, woodworkers, and textile artists. It’s a premier spot for finding high-quality, locally-made home goods.
Live Entertainment: There is almost always a live band or solo performer playing near the entrance, contributing to the high-energy, community-driven vibe that defines East Van.
https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/trout-lake-farmers-market-fresh-strawberries-in-summer-gm2165608971-585792915
Key Information
Location: North parking lot of John Hendry Park (between Lakewood Drive and Templeton Drive).
Season: Typically runs from early May through late October.
Hours: Saturdays, 9:00 AM – 2:00 PM.
Access: A short walk from the Commercial-Broadway SkyTrain station. If you are biking, it is perfectly situated along the Central Valley Greenway.
Payment: Most vendors are set up for mobile tap payments; the market info booth also handles the "Market Money" program for card-to-token exchanges.
Tips
This is arguably the busiest market in the city. To avoid the peak crowds and ensure you get the best selection of popular items like fresh berries or sourdough, arrive right at 9:00 AM.
The small lot fills up instantly, and street parking in the surrounding residential blocks is very limited. Public transit or cycling is highly recommended.
The market is very popular with families. If you have a dog, keep them on a short leash as the aisles can become very congested during the 11:00 AM – 1:00 PM rush.
While there are a few picnic tables, they are usually claimed quickly. Bringing a small foldable stool or a picnic blanket allows you to enjoy the food trucks comfortably in the park.

places.name: UBC Farm Saturday Farmers’ Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/close-up-and-textures-of-freshly-harvested-organic-potatoes-and-yams-at-trout-lake-gm2166549062-586648337

The UBC Farm Saturday Farmers’ Market is widely considered the crown jewel of Vancouver’s market scene. It is the only multi-vendor market in the city located on an actual working farm, offering a rustic, forest-fringed escape right on the UBC South Campus.
What to Expect
Authentic Farm Vibe: Located on a 24-hectare working research farm, providing a rustic, forest-fringed escape within the city.
Organic Produce: Features a wide array of UBC Farm’s own certified organic fruits, vegetables, and unique heirloom varieties.
Diverse Vendors: Host to over 30 local partners selling artisanal spirits, craft beer, fresh-baked bread, handmade jewelry, and sustainably raised meats.
Live Atmosphere: Often features live music and a community-centric environment that feels more like a weekend retreat than a grocery run.
Educational Tours: Regular opportunities for by-donation farm tours to learn about sustainable agriculture and the research being conducted on-site.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early June through late October.
Day: Every Saturday, rain or shine.
Hours: 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM.
Location: 3461 Ross Drive, Vancouver (UBC South Campus).
Payment: Vendors typically accept Cash, Debit, Visa, and Mastercard.
Pet Policy: Leashed dogs are permitted within the designated market area.
Parking: Limited free 2-hour parking available at the main gate; additional overflow parking is located in nearby Wesbrook Village.
Tips
Check social media for U-Pick berry announcements; these sessions are popular and rows often clear out quickly.
Utilize the #68 bus for direct access or bike through Pacific Spirit Park to avoid parking congestion.
Bring your own reusable bags, containers, and even a wagon for heavy hauls, as the market emphasizes a zero-waste approach.
View the weekly Fresh Sheet on the UBC Farm website prior to visiting to see exactly what is being harvested.
Grab a coffee and snack from the on-site food trucks and enjoy them in the apple orchard seating area.

places.name: West End Farmers’ Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/view-of-sign-west-end-farmers-market-in-downtown-vancouver-gm1310667043-399996594
Tucked between high-rises and the lush greenery of Nelson Park, this market offers a relaxed, community-focused atmosphere in the heart of the city.
What to Expect
Local Variety: Features over 30 vendors providing a curated selection of seasonal fruits and vegetables, pasture-raised meats, fresh fish, and farm-fresh eggs.
Artisanal Finds: Plenty of stalls offering small-batch preserves, honey, artisanal cheeses, and freshly baked sourdough and pastries.
Craft Beverages: A great spot to find local BC craft beer, wine, and spirits directly from the producers.
Parkside Amenities: The adjacent park, playground, and community gardens make it an ideal spot for a post-shopping picnic or a family outing.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from late May through late October.
Day: Every Saturday, rain or shine.
Hours: 9:00 AM – 2:00 PM.
Location: 1100 Comox Street (between Bute and Thurlow Streets), Vancouver.
Payment: Most vendors are equipped for Debit, Visa, and Mastercard, though carrying some cash is helpful for smaller quick transactions.
Pet Policy: Well-behaved, leashed dogs are welcome to join you as you browse.
Parking: No designated market parking lot. Street parking is very limited and mostly restricted to residents; metered stalls can be found on nearby Davie, Burrard, or Thurlow Streets.
Tips
Pick up fresh bread, cheese, and seasonal fruit at the market, then walk a few steps into Nelson Park to enjoy an al fresco lunch.
Given the difficult parking situation in the West End, arriving by foot, TransLink, or a Mobi bike-share is the most stress-free option.
This is a popular neighborhood hub; for the best choice of popular items like fresh berries or specialty greens, aim to arrive before 10:30 AM.
Like other Vancouver markets, vendors encourage a plastic-bag-free environment. Bring your own reusable totes or mesh produce bags.
Use the market as a starting point to explore the local boutiques on Bute Street or the diverse eateries along Davie Street.

places.name: Burnaby Artisan Farmers' Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/freshly-harvested-organic-warba-potatoes-at-trout-lake-farmers-market-in-british-gm2166548895-586648312

The Burnaby Artisan Farmers’ Market is a well-established community fixture located at the heart of the city’s civic center. Set against the backdrop of Deer Lake Park, this market is celebrated for its balanced mix of conventional and organic produce, professional artisans, and its commitment to creating a welcoming weekend tradition for North Burnaby families.
What to Expect
Community Atmosphere: A medium-sized market that strikes a perfect balance—large enough for a diverse selection, but intimate enough to avoid overwhelming crowds.
Handcrafted Focus: True to its artisan name, you will find a significant number of local crafters and makers alongside traditional farm stalls.
Local Flavours: Features a rotating lineup of conventional and organic produce, wild foragers, artisan bakers, and hot food service vendors.
Family Friendly: Often includes live entertainment and kid-friendly activities, making it a popular Saturday morning destination for local families.
Proximity to Landmarks: Located near popular Burnaby spots like Deer Lake Park and the Burnaby Village Museum, allowing for a full day of local sightseeing.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early May through late October.
Day: Every Saturday, rain or shine.
Hours: 9:00 AM – 2:00 PM.

Location: Traditionally held in the North Parking Lot at Burnaby City Hall (4949 Canada Way). Note: Always check local listings as venue changes occasionally occur due to city hall construction or events.
Payment: Most vendors accept major credit cards and debit; a central market tent often provides "market money" tokens in exchange for debit if needed.
Pet Policy: Dogs are generally welcome on a leash, but it is recommended to keep them to the outer edges of the vendor stalls during peak busy hours.
Tips
After shopping, drive two minutes down the road to Deer Lake Park. It’s the perfect place to enjoy any fresh pastries or snacks you picked up at the market.
Unlike downtown markets, the City Hall location typically offers ample free parking, making it one of the most accessible markets for those arriving by car.
Keep an eye out for special events, such as the Halloween-themed market in late October or seasonal Holiday Hive pop-ups.
The artisan bakers here are highly popular; if you have your heart set on a specific sourdough or specialty loaf, aim to arrive within the first hour.
The market is accessible via several bus routes along Canada Way and is a short connector bus ride from the Sperling–Burnaby Lake SkyTrain station.

places.name: Brentwood Artisan Farmers’ Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/try-a-sample-close-up-of-freshly-harvested-organic-blueberry-compostable-container-gm2166548945-586648356

The Brentwood Artisan Farmers’ Market is a newer addition to the local scene, bringing a fresh, outdoor shopping experience to the bustling area surrounding The Amazing Brentwood. It serves as a modern Sunday destination where urban lifestyle meets local agriculture.
What to Expect
Modern Urban Setting: Held along Brentwood Boulevard, the market offers a vibrant, open-air atmosphere set against the backdrop of one of Burnaby’s most high-profile developments.
Handpicked Selection: Features a rotating collective of roughly 30+ vendors, ranging from organic and conventional farmers to local bakers and foragers.
Artisan Makers: True to its name, there is a strong focus on high-quality handcrafted goods, including ceramics, jewelry, and apothecary items.
Grab-and-Go Eats: A curated selection of prepared food vendors and food trucks make it a popular spot for a Sunday brunch or lunch on the go.
Lively Vibe: The market frequently hosts live local musicians, adding a rhythmic, energetic feel to your morning shop.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early June through late September.
Day: Every Sunday, rain or shine.
Hours: 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM.
Location: Brentwood Boulevard (between Halifax Way and Alpha Ave), Burnaby.
Payment: Most vendors are set up for contactless payment (Debit/Credit), though carrying cash is still recommended for smaller farm stalls.
Pet Policy: Being an outdoor street market, well-behaved leashed dogs are generally welcome.
Tips
Located just steps from the Brentwood Town Centre SkyTrain Station, arriving by transit is the most efficient way to visit.
Since the market is right at The Amazing Brentwood, you can easily combine your local farm shopping with a visit to the mall’s larger retailers or the TABLES food court.
This specific market can get quite warm in the summer sun due to the surrounding pavement; bring a water bottle and take advantage of the shaded seating areas nearby.
As an outdoor seasonal market, the atmosphere changes with the temperature. Arrive right at 10:00 AM during peak summer weeks to shop before the midday heat.
The area is bike-friendly with dedicated racks available throughout the Brentwood development.

places.name: Coquitlam Farmers Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/freshly-harvested-organic-carrots-and-shallots-with-backdrop-of-wood-crate-at-trout-gm2166548887-586648307

The Coquitlam Farmers Market holds the distinction of being the longest-running suburban farmers market in the Lower Mainland. It serves as a major community anchor for the Tri-Cities, offering a spacious and organized shopping experience.
What to Expect
Established Community Hub: A large, well-attended market that has been a staple for Coquitlam residents since 1996.
Farm-to-Table Focus: Strong representation from Fraser Valley farmers providing seasonal berries, stone fruits, greenhouse greens, and root vegetables.
Prepared Gourmet Goods: Features an extensive selection of kitchen table items including small-batch preserves, local honey, fresh pastas, and ethnic prepared foods.
Artisan Alley: Dedicated space for local crafters selling handmade soaps, pottery, textiles, and jewelry.
Entertainment & Events: Regularly features live music, cooking demonstrations, and Kids’ Club activities to keep younger visitors engaged.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early May through late October.
Day: Every Sunday, rain or shine.
Hours: 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM.
Location: Dogwood Pavilion Parking Lot (1655 Winslow Ave), Coquitlam.
Payment: Most vendors accept Debit and Credit; the Market Manager tent also sells market tokens for those needing to use a card for cash-only stalls.
Pet Policy: Leashed dogs are welcome but are encouraged to visit during the quieter first and last hours of the market.
Tips for Success
The market is located across from the Poirier Sport & Leisure Complex and the Coquitlam Public Library, making it easy to combine your grocery shopping with a swim, skate, or book pickup.
One of the easiest markets to access by car, with significant free parking available in the surrounding Dogwood and Poirier lots.
The most popular produce and fresh eggs often sell out within the first 90 minutes.
Many prepared food vendors participate in waste-reduction initiatives; bringing your own egg cartons and berry baskets is highly encouraged.
The market layout is consistent, but checking the digital vendor map on their website before arriving helps you navigate quickly to your favorite stalls.

places.name: Ladner Village Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/freshly-harvested-organic-sieglinde-potatoes-at-trout-lake-farmers-market-in-british-gm2166548993-586648359

The Ladner Village Market is one of the largest open-air markets in Western Canada, spanning three blocks in the heart of historic Ladner. Known for its Make it, Bake it, Grow it philosophy, it offers a massive festival-like atmosphere that draws visitors from across the Lower Mainland.
What to Expect
Grand Scale: With over 200 vendors per date, this is more of a community event than a simple market, covering 48th Avenue from Delta Street to Elliott Street.
Handmade Quality: A strict focus on local artisans and producers ensures you are buying directly from the person who made, baked, or grew the product.
Live Entertainment: Multiple stages featuring local musicians provide a continuous soundtrack to your shopping experience.
Heritage Charm: The market is set against the backdrop of Ladner’s historic fishing village, offering a quaint, small-town feel despite its large size.
Diverse Selection: Beyond fresh produce, expect high-end woodworking, gourmet food trucks, soaps, clothing, and local BC wines and spirits.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early June through early September.
Day: Select Sundays (typically the second and fourth Sunday of the month).
Hours: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM.
Location: 48th Avenue, Ladner Village, Delta.
Payment: Most vendors accept card payments, but cash is very helpful for faster service at busy farm stalls.
Pet Policy: No dogs permitted. Due to the high density of crowds and hot pavement, the market maintains a strict no-pet policy (service animals excepted).
Tips
Unlike many other regional markets, Ladner is not dog-friendly. Avoid disappointment by leaving pets at home, as they are not permitted within the market boundaries.
Street parking is free but fills up almost immediately. Look for spots at Memorial Park (47 Ave) or use the secondary lots at local schools and churches within a 5-10 minute walk.
Because the market only happens twice a month, it gets incredibly busy. Arriving at 10:00 AM allows you to browse the most popular artisans before the midday rush.
Given the sheer number of vendors, most people leave with more than they planned. A wagon or a large backpack is highly recommended for navigating the three-block stretch.
Many of the permanent boutiques and cafes along 48th Avenue open specifically for market Sundays; it's a great time to explore the local brick-and-mortar businesses of Ladner.

places.name: North Delta Farmers Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/green-and-yellow-zucchini-potatoes-at-trout-lake-farmers-market-in-british-columbia-gm2166548930-586648370

The North Delta Farmers Market is a thriving community hub that brings the best of BC’s agriculture and artisanal talent to the heart of the Sunshine Hills neighborhood. Known for its friendly, welcoming atmosphere, it is a key Sunday destination for families in Delta and Surrey.
What to Expect
Direct-from-Farm Produce: Features a rotating selection of seasonal fruits and vegetables, with a strong emphasis on crops from the nearby Fraser Valley.
Artisan Diversity: A wide array of "Make it, Bake it, Grow it" vendors, including local jewelry makers, soap crafters, and textile artists.
Gourmet Prepared Foods: Offers everything from small-batch hot sauces and honey to freshly made salsas and traditional baked goods.
Rotating Food Trucks: Each week features different local food trucks, providing various lunch options ranging from plant-based bowls to authentic international street food.
Community Spirit: The market often includes a community tent where local non-profits and neighborhood groups share information and host interactive activities.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from mid-May through late October.
Day: Every Sunday, rain or shine.
Hours: 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM.
Location: North Delta Recreation Centre parking lot (11415 84 Ave), Delta.
Payment: Most vendors are equipped for Debit and Credit; cash is always useful for smaller transactions.
Pet Policy: Leashed, well-behaved dogs are welcome to accompany their owners through the market aisles.
Tips for Success

Since the market is located at the North Delta Recreation Centre, you can easily combine your visit with the nearby playground, skate park, or a walk through the trails of Sungod Recreation Centre nearby.
Popular items like local eggs, sourdough, and seasonal berries tend to sell out by noon; aim for an 10:00 AM arrival for the best variety.
Follow their social media pages for Vendor Spotlights posted every Friday to see which specific makers and food trucks will be appearing that Sunday.
Several bus routes (including the #312 and #316) stop directly near the Recreation Centre, making it a convenient car-free trip for North Delta and Surrey residents.
In line with local sustainability goals, vendors appreciate shoppers who bring their own totes, produce bags, and egg cartons.

places.name: Southlands Grange Farmers Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/close-up-of-freshly-harvested-organic-beets-at-trout-lake-farmers-market-in-british-gm2166548891-586648316

The Southlands Grange Farmers Market is one of the most unique additions to the Lower Mainland’s market circuit. Located within a boutique agricultural community in Boundary Bay, it offers a sophisticated yet rustic experience that feels like a modern farm estate.
What to Expect
Modern Farmscape: Set in the beautifully designed Southlands community, the market takes place around the historic Grange building and a central pedestrian plaza.
Curated Quality: A highly selective boutique feel with vendors offering premium organic produce, pasture-raised meats, and high-end artisanal goods.
Culinary Focus: Features a strong presence of gourmet prepared foods, including wood-fired breads, specialty preserves, and small-batch pantry staples.
Agri-Hood Atmosphere: Unlike urban markets, this is set against active farmland and community gardens, providing a seamless connection between the market and the fields.
Lifestyle Destination: The market is often paired with lifestyle workshops, gardening talks, or live acoustic music, making it a sophisticated Sunday outing.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early May through early November.
Day: Bi-weekly Saturdays (every other week).
Hours: 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM.
Location: The Market Square at Southlands (6333 Market Ave), Delta.
Payment: Most vendors accept major credit and debit cards; contactless payment is the standard here.
Pet Policy: Dogs are welcome on a leash throughout the plaza and surrounding walking trails.
Tips for Success
After shopping, take a walk through the adjacent Southlands forest trails or bike down to nearby Boundary Bay Regional Park and Centennial Beach.
The permanent Prado Café located right on the square is a popular hub; grab a coffee before the market starts to beat the morning rush.
Southlands is designed to be highly accessible by bike from the Boundary Bay trail system. There is ample bike parking near the Grange.
The Grange often hosts agricultural or craft workshops (like floral arranging or sourdough baking) on market days; check their online calendar to book ahead.
The market square is beautifully sunlit; if you prefer a quieter experience, the final hour (1:00 PM – 2:00 PM) offers a more relaxed pace and great lighting for photos.

places.name: Kwantlen Farmers’ Markethttps://www.istockphoto.com/photo/peach-gm1283056463-380603927
body: The Kwantlen Farmers’ Market is a unique community gathering spot that bridges the gap between Richmond’s urban center and its rich agricultural roots. Hosted in partnership with the Kwantlen Student Association, it serves as a vital link for local food security and sustainable farming.
What to Expect
Student and Community Hub: A diverse and energetic atmosphere where university students, local families, and urban gardeners converge.
Hyper-Local Produce: Features a strong selection of Richmond-grown vegetables and fruits, including seasonal specialties from the nearby Richmond Agricultural Land Reserve.
Incubator Spirit: Often serves as a launching pad for new, small-scale local entrepreneurs, meaning you’ll find innovative snacks, crafts, and unique artisanal products.
International Flavors: Reflecting Richmond’s cultural diversity, the market often features a wide range of prepared ethnic foods and fusion treats.
Educational Focus: Regular appearances by community groups and university programs offering tips on urban farming, composting, and sustainable living.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from late spring through early autumn.
Day: Every Tuesday, rain or shine.
Hours: 12:00 PM – 4:00 PM.
Location: Kwantlen Polytechnic University (KPU) Richmond Campus (8771 Lansdowne Rd), Richmond.
Payment: Most vendors accept major credit and debit cards; carrying some cash is recommended for smaller, farm-direct purchases.
Pet Policy: Leashed, well-behaved dogs are welcome in the outdoor market area.
Tips
Because this is a Tuesday market, it is the perfect spot to restock your fridge mid-week without the massive weekend crowds found at other regional markets.
The market is located just a short walk from the Lansdowne Canada Line Station, making it one of the most transit-accessible markets in the Lower Mainland.
Since the campus is directly across from Lansdowne Centre, you can easily pair your farmers' market visit with a trip to larger retail stores or the mall’s food district.
The noon start time makes this a popular destination for local office workers and students to grab a fresh, locally-sourced lunch from the rotating food trucks.
While transit is recommended, there is paid parking available in the KPU Richmond lot and surrounding street meters. Be sure to check the signage for campus-specific parking regulations.

places.name: Steveston Farmers’ and Artisans’ Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/organic-farmers-market-okanagan-valley-gm1160059283-317428567

The Steveston Farmers’ and Artisans’ Market is a premier Sunday destination that perfectly captures the coastal charm of Richmond’s historic fishing village. Following a recent move due to local construction, the market has found a beautiful new home at Garry Point Park, offering shoppers stunning waterfront views alongside fresh local goods.
What to Expect
Scenic Waterfront Atmosphere: Located at the entrance to Steveston Village, the market provides a refreshing breeze and views of the Fraser River as you shop.
Make It, Bake It, Grow It, Catch It: The market strictly adheres to a local-first philosophy, ensuring every product is farmed, caught, or handcrafted in British Columbia.
Gourmet Coastal Eats: Given its location, you can often find unique items like fresh local seafood, small-batch preserves, and artisanal honey.
Artisans & Makers: A high concentration of local artists selling unique jewelry, pottery, textiles, and woodworking, making it an excellent spot for gift shopping.
Live Local Music: The market features a dedicated stage for local performers, creating a social, festival-like environment that encourages lingering.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from mid-May through mid-October.
Day: Bi-weekly Sundays (every other week).
Hours: 10:30 AM – 3:30 PM.
Location: Garry Point Park (7th Avenue at Moncton Street), Steveston Village, Richmond.
Payment: Vendors are generally equipped for contactless Debit and Credit payments; cash is always a safe backup for smaller produce stalls.
Pet Policy: Well-behaved, leashed dogs are welcome, making it a favorite for pet owners walking the Garry Point trails.
Tips
Before or after shopping, take the loop trail around the park for panoramic views of the Gulf Islands and the Salish Sea.
Use the market as a base to visit nearby National Historic Sites like the Gulf of Georgia Cannery or the Britannia Shipyards.
Steveston is a major tourist draw on sunny Sundays. Arriving right at 10:30 AM helps you secure better parking and the first pick of fresh bakery items.
Between the market stalls and the village boardwalks, you’ll likely do a lot of walking. Wear comfortable shoes and bring a reusable tote for your hauls.
In late summer, keep an eye out for Richmond’s famous corn on the cob and berries, which are often the stars of the produce section.

places.name: New West Farmers’ Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/view-of-apples-for-sales-on-the-street-market-in-new-westminster-gm1440972667-480795460

The New West Farmers’ Market is a vibrant community staple set in the heart of Uptown New Westminster. Known for its inclusive and festive atmosphere, it transforms the park into a bustling marketplace that highlights the best of BC’s local growers and makers.
What to Expect
Tiered Garden Setting: The market is held in the beautiful Tipperary Park, featuring a scenic layout with pathways that wind through various vendor sections.
Alcohol & Artisan Spirits: One of the best markets for sampling and purchasing BC craft beer, wine, cider, and spirits directly from local distillers.
Diverse Food Scene: Reflecting the city's demographic, you’ll find a wide range of prepared foods including authentic pierogies, tamales, and diverse vegan and gluten-free options.
The "Busker Station": A dedicated area for local musicians ensures a lively, upbeat soundtrack for your weekly grocery shop.
Kids’ Programming: Often features a "Kids' Market" or "Power of Produce" (PoP) club where children can learn about seasonal eating and earn tokens for fresh fruit and vegetables.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early April through early November.
Day: Every Thursday, rain or shine.
Hours: 3:00 PM – 7:00 PM.
Location: Tipperary Park (315 Queens Ave), New Westminster.
Payment: Most vendors accept major credit and debit cards; "Market Money" tokens can be purchased at the information tent using a debit card.
Pet Policy: Leashed, friendly dogs are permitted and very common at this neighborhood-friendly market.
Tips for Success
Since the market runs on Thursday evenings, it is the ideal spot to pick up fresh ingredients for dinner on your way home from work.
The market is about a 10-minute walk (uphill) from the New Westminster SkyTrain Station or a quick ride on the #106 or #123 bus.
Many shoppers grab dinner from the rotating food trucks and enjoy it on the grass or at the park benches overlooking the market.
Some vendors offer discounts for bringing your own cup for coffee or lemonade, aligning with the market's strong sustainability focus.
Keep an eye out for themed evenings, such as the Harvest Festival in October or Pride at the Market in August, which often include extra activities and decorations.

places.name: Loutet Farm Community Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/jars-of-pickled-onion-and-pickled-cucumber-in-a-jar-at-trout-lake-farmers-market-in-gm2166548969-586648379

The Loutet Farm Community Market is a unique farm-gate style market located on North Vancouver’s first urban farm. Unlike traditional markets that host outside vendors, this market is centered around the hyper-local harvest from Loutet Farm itself, a social enterprise that transforms underutilized parkland into a thriving agricultural hub.
What to Expect
Hyper-Seasonal Variety: Because it is a working farm, the selection changes weekly based on what is at peak harvest, ranging from crisp spring radishes to hearty autumn kale.
Sustainability Focus: A deeply eco-conscious atmosphere where the community gathers to support urban agriculture and learn about sustainable food systems.
Intimate Vibe: Smaller and more focused than the massive regional markets, it offers a quiet, neighborhood-centric shopping experience.
Educational Outreach: The farm often hosts staff who can answer questions about urban gardening, composting, and the specific varieties of heirloom vegetables they grow.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from May through October.
Day: Every Saturday, rain or shine.
Hours: 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM.
Location: Loutet Farm (14th Street & Rufus Avenue), North Vancouver.
Payment: Primarily Debit and Credit; cash is accepted and helpful for smaller farm-direct purchases.
Pet Policy: Leashed dogs are welcome in the market area but are not permitted in the active growing rows of the farm.
Tips
Located in the heart of a residential neighborhood, the market is easily accessible via the North Shore Spirit Trail and local bike paths.
Consistent with their sustainability mission, this is a strictly "bring your own bag" market; vendors do not provide plastic.
The farm’s signature salad blends and fresh herbs are highly sought after and often sell out within the first hour.
While staying on the designated paths, take a moment to walk the perimeter of the farm to see exactly where your food was grown.
If you're a local, ask at the info tent about Volunteer Harvest days, which are a great way to get involved with the community.

places.name: Market at the Quay Farmers’ Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/vibrant-a-frame-sign-for-lonsdale-quay-farmers-market-in-north-vancouver-gm2239978786-654742553

The Market at the Quay Farmers’ Market (also known as the Lonsdale Quay Farmers’ Market) is a beloved North Vancouver tradition that brings the farm to the waterfront. Located along the scenic boardwalk of Lonsdale Quay, this evening market offers a refined, coastal shopping experience where you can enjoy the ocean breeze while browsing fresh BC produce and handmade artisan goods.
What to Expect
Iconic Waterfront Setting: Held at the Shipyards District, this market offers breathtaking views of the Vancouver skyline and the bustling Burrard Inlet.
Artisan and Farm Fusion: A diverse mix of Sea-to-Sky corridor farmers and North Shore artisans selling handmade jewelry, ceramics, and textiles.
Prepared Gourmet Goods: Features an impressive array of local preserves, artisanal honey, small-batch spirits, and fresh-baked sourdough.
Entertainment Hub: Often synchronized with live music or community events at Lonsdale Quay, creating a festive, high-energy environment.
Indoor-Outdoor Flexibility: Being adjacent to Lonsdale Quay Market, you can easily pivot between the outdoor farmers' stalls and the permanent indoor vendors.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from late May through late October.
Day: Every Wednesday, rain or shine.
Hours: 3:00 PM – 7:00 PM.
Location: The Shipyards / Lonsdale Quay (123 Carrie Cates Ct), North Vancouver.
Payment: Most vendors are equipped for contactless card payments; the market info desk can often provide assistance with debit-to-token exchanges.
Pet Policy: Leashed dogs are very common and welcome in the open-air plaza.
Tips
The market is located just steps from the Lonsdale Quay SeaBus Terminal, making it the easiest car-free market to visit from downtown Vancouver.
If driving, use the ICBC parking garage (free on weekends) or the Lonsdale Quay Market underground lot.
Grab a snack from a market vendor or a meal from one of the many restaurants in the Shipyards District and enjoy it on the Big Yellow Megaphone deck.
If visiting on select summer weekends, check if the Friday Night Market is also running for a completely different festive vibe.
The waterfront can be significantly breezier and cooler than inland areas; bring a light jacket even on sunny days.

places.name: Langley Community Farmers’ Market – Douglas Park
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/flowers-and-vegetables-trout-lake-farmers-market-east-vancouver-canada-gm547138192-98806717

The Langley Community Farmers’ Market at Douglas Park provides a central, highly accessible mid-week shopping option in the heart of Langley City. This location is known for its intimate, community-focused vibe and its commitment to providing market to table access right in the urban core.
What to Expect
Hyper-Local Focus: Features a strong presence of Langley-based growers, offering everything from fresh-cut flowers to seasonal Fraser Valley fruits and vegetables.
Mid-Week Convenience: Designed as a Wednesday afternoon hub, it serves as an ideal spot for locals to restock their kitchens before the weekend.
Family Fun: The park setting includes a permanent playground and water park, making it a favorite for parents shopping with young children.
Live Entertainment: Local musicians often perform at the park’s permanent stage, creating a relaxed, small-town community vibe.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early June through late August.
Day: Every Wednesday, rain or shine.
Hours: 5:30 PM – 8:30 PM.
Location: Douglas Park (20550 Douglas Crescent), Langley City.
Payment: Most vendors accept major credit and debit cards; carrying some cash is helpful for quick produce purchases.
Pet Policy: Well-behaved, leashed dogs are welcome in the park and market area.
Tips
If you are traveling through Langley, aim to arrive right at 3:00 PM to shop before the evening rush hour traffic peaks.
Pick up some fresh pastries, berries, and artisanal cheese, then claim a spot on the grass to enjoy dinner while listening to the local buskers.
Street parking is available around the perimeter of the park, and there is a public lot located at the nearby Timms Community Centre.
Being an outdoor market under large trees, it stays cool on hot days, but can be damp after rain; wear appropriate footwear for grass.

places.name: Langley Community Farmers’ Market – Langley Events Centre
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/display-of-fresh-ripe-organic-broccoli-at-the-weekend-farmers-market-gm1166706231-321480312

The Langley Community Farmers’ Market at the Langley Events Centre (LEC) is a massive regional powerhouse that combines agriculture with local lifestyle. Its spacious layout and high-energy atmosphere make it one of the largest and most accessible weekday markets in the valley, serving as a significant hub for those living in the Willoughby and Walnut Grove areas.
What to Expect
Agriculture Meets Athletics: A unique blend of shoppers, ranging from local food enthusiasts to families visiting for sports tournaments.
Regional Powerhouse: Often features a larger number of vendors than the mid-week market, including specialty meat producers, local wineries, and craft breweries.
Prepared Food Focus: A fantastic selection of food trucks and prepared meal vendors, making it a top choice for a Sunday brunch outing.
Artisan Diversity: Host to a rotating cast of local makers selling handmade home decor, clothing, and natural skincare products.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early June through late August.
Day: Every Thursday (Note: For 2026, the Sunday schedule has shifted to a mid-week evening format at this location).
Hours: 5:30 PM – 8:30 PM.
Location: Langley Events Centre (7888 200 St), Langley.
Payment: Most vendors are equipped for contactless payments; the market information tent provides assistance if needed.
Pet Policy: Leashed dogs are permitted in the market area.
Tips
This is one of the easiest markets for parking, with the massive LEC lots providing plenty of free space for visitors.
Because the LEC market is quite large, checking their social media or website for the weekly layout can save you time.
If you plan on attending a game or event at the LEC after shopping, bring an insulated cooler bag to keep your produce and dairy fresh in the car.
The flat, paved surface of the parking lot makes this market one of the most accessible for strollers and mobility aids.

places.name: Fort Langley Village Farmers’ Markethttps://www.istockphoto.com/photo/shopping-at-fort-langley-village-farmers-market-canada-gm1163816159-319697187
body: The Fort Langley Village Farmers’ Market offers a heritage-rich shopping experience with its location next to the historic St. Andrew’s United Church. This curated market emphasizes small-batch organic goods and artisan crafts within a picturesque village setting, making it a favorite for those seeking a slower, more intentional pace.
What to Expect
Organic & Small-Batch: A high concentration of organic farmers from the Glen Valley and surrounding areas, alongside artisanal bakers and foragers.
Authentic Village Vibe: This market maintains a strict "Produce of BC" and "Handmade" focus, ensuring a high-quality, curated shopping experience.
Scenic Surroundings: Surrounded by 19th-century architecture and boutique shops, it offers a picturesque backdrop for a weekend outing.
Curated Artisans: Features unique local finds such as hand-spun wool, artisanal preserves, and local honey that reflect the region's agricultural history.
https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/market-day-in-fort-langley-canada-gm1163816162-319697189
https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/summer-market-in-langley-canada-gm1012138364-272676596
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early May through late October.
Day: Every Saturday, rain or shine.
Hours: 9:00 AM – 3:00 PM.
Location: St. Andrew’s United Church (9025 Glover Rd), Fort Langley.
Payment: Vendors typically accept Debit and Credit; cash is still widely used and appreciated here.
Pet Policy: Leashed dogs are welcome, though the aisles can become very crowded during the lunch hour.
Tips
Fort Langley is a major weekend destination. For the best parking spots, aim to arrive before 9:30 AM; otherwise, look for parking near the Fort Langley Community Hall.
After the market, take a stroll down Glover Road to explore the many independent bookstores, antique shops, and cafes.
Make it a full day trip by visiting the Fort Langley National Historic Site, located just a short walk from the market.
In keeping with the village's rustic charm and sustainability efforts, shoppers are encouraged to bring their own baskets or sturdy totes.
The fresh fruit pies and sourdough loaves found here are legendary; they often sell out well before the market closes at 3:00 PM.

places.name: White Rock Farmers’ Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/a-local-with-pink-bag-shopping-organic-kale-at-trout-lake-farmers-market-in-british-gm2166548940-586648371

The White Rock Farmers’ Market is one of the most celebrated markets in British Columbia, consistently winning awards for its size, variety, and community atmosphere. Located in the heart of the city near the iconic Miramar Village, it offers a lively festival feel that draws visitors from across the Semiahmoo Peninsula.
What to Expect
Award-Winning Scale: Frequently voted one of the best markets in the province, hosting over 80 vendors during the peak of the season.
Diverse Agriculture: A massive selection of Fraser Valley produce, including everything from organic berries and greenhouse peppers to farm-fresh eggs and honey.
Gourmet Hot Food: A high-end food truck and prepared-food scene featuring local favorites like gourmet pierogies, artisan pizzas, and freshly roasted coffee.
The Artisan Plaza: A dedicated area for professional makers selling high-quality jewelry, woodworking, hand-poured candles, and original West Coast art.
Live Cultural Performances: Features a central stage that hosts a rotating schedule of local musicians, adding a rhythmic, upbeat energy to the Sunday morning routine.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from late April through late October.
Day: Every Sunday, rain or shine.
Hours: 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM.
Location: Miramar Village / Whaling Wall (Russell Avenue and Johnston Road), White Rock.
Payment: Most vendors accept Debit and Credit; the market info tent sells "Market Money" tokens for those who need them.
Pet Policy: Leashed, well-behaved dogs are welcome to join you through the market stalls.
Tips
After stocking up on groceries, drive or walk five minutes down the hill to the White Rock Pier and Promenade for a stroll by the ocean.
Free parking is available at the White Rock City Hall lot and the Whaling Wall parkade. During peak summer weeks, arriving by 9:45 AM is the best way to secure a spot.
Since this market is large and the weather in White Rock is often warm, keep a cooler in your car to ensure your meats, cheeses, and berries stay fresh while you explore the local shops.
Don't miss the massive Wyland mural adjacent to the market—it’s a great landmark for meeting up with friends or taking a quick photo.
With 80+ vendors, it can be easy to miss a specific stall. Check the market’s website or the large chalkboard at the entrance for the weekly layout and a list of New This Week vendors.

places.name: Abbotsford Farm & Country Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/blueberries-strawberries-organic-gm507620291-45898900

The Abbotsford Farm & Country Market is the city’s longest-running market, located in the heart of Canada’s most productive agricultural region. It delivers produce that is famously fresh and local, maintaining a historic downtown charm while showcasing the best of the Fraser Valley's large-scale farms and artisan creators.
What to Expect

True Agricultural Roots: As a hub in one of Canada’s most productive agricultural regions, the market features a massive selection of farm-fresh produce, including berries, corn, and greenhouse greens.
Handmade & Homegrown: Strictly follows a Real Farmers, Real Food philosophy, featuring local bakers, meat producers, and foragers alongside traditional farm stalls.
Artisan Makers: A rotating lineup of local entertainers and artisans selling unique crafts, wearable accessories, and handmade home goods.
Community Events: Often hosts prize giveaways, live music, and special seasonal events that make it a social cornerstone for the Fraser Valley.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early May through late October.
Day: Every Saturday, rain or shine.
Hours: 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM.
Location: Jubilee Park (2552 McCallum Road), Abbotsford.
Payment: Most vendors are equipped for Debit and Credit; cash is widely accepted and useful for smaller farm-direct purchases.
Pet Policy: Dogs are generally welcome on leashes, though it is recommended to keep them to the outer edges during the busy mid-morning peak.
Tips
The market is perfectly situated for a post-shopping stroll through Downtown Abbotsford to visit local favorites like Lepp’s Daily Market or the boutiques on Montrose Avenue.
Ample parking is available in the surrounding street spots and public lots, but arriving early (before 10:00 AM) ensures a spot closest to the park.
Since you’re in the heart of farm country, pair your visit with a trip to nearby Maan Farms or Taves Family Farms for seasonal activities like u-pick or corn mazes.
Vendors prioritize sustainability and often do not provide bags; a sturdy wagon is a great idea if you plan on stocking up on heavy items like flats of berries or squash.
In early summer, keep an eye out for local tulips from the nearby festivals, and in August, look for Abbotsford’s world-famous sweet corn.

places.name: Downtown Chilliwack Community Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/organic-farmers-market-penticton-okanagan-valley-gm871718020-243512298

The is a non-profit, community-driven hub located in the revitalized heart of Chilliwack. As a certified BC Association of Farmers' Markets (BCAFM) member, it operates under a strict "Make it, Bake it, Grow it" policy, ensuring that every item is local, authentic, and high-quality.
What to Expect
Authentic Local Goods: A guarantee that everything sold—from crisp seasonal produce to intricate art—is grown or crafted by the person behind the table.
Community-First Atmosphere: As a non-profit, the market’s focus is on food security and local connection; every dollar spent supports the regional economy and community initiatives.
Artisanal Variety: Beyond farm-fresh fruits and vegetables, expect to find handcrafted soaps, small-batch preserves, unique textiles, and professional-grade jewelry.
Central Gathering Point: Located in a bustling downtown park, the market often features live music and community tables, making it a social anchor for the weekend.
Urban Revitalization: The market provides a perfect opportunity to see the ongoing transformation of downtown Chilliwack, blending historic charm with modern community energy.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from late May through late October.
Day: Every Saturday, rain or shine.
Hours: 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM.
Location: Central Community Park (45951 Victoria Ave), Chilliwack.
Payment: Most vendors are equipped for Debit and Credit; cash is always useful and appreciated for smaller farm purchases.
Pet Policy: Friendly, leashed dogs are welcome to join their owners in the park.
Tips
After you finish your market shopping, walk over to the nearby District 1881, a walkable cultural hub filled with local breweries, boutiques, and eateries.
While there is street parking available, looking for spots in the public lots a block or two away often saves time during the busy mid-morning rush.
Central Community Park features plenty of green space and a splash pad nearby, making it easy to keep kids entertained while you browse.
Chilliwack is famous for its corn and berries; arrive at 10:00 AM sharp during peak season to secure the best of the day’s harvest before they sell out.
Like most BC markets, shoppers are encouraged to bring their own reusable bags and containers to help reduce the market's environmental footprint.

places.name: Mission City Farmers’ Markethttps://www.istockphoto.com/photo/close-up-of-freshly-harvested-organic-beets-at-trout-lake-farmers-market-in-british-gm2166548943-586648343
body: The Mission City Farmers’ Market is a long-standing community staple celebrating its 30th season in 2026. Located in the picturesque Centennial Park, it provides a scenic backdrop for a Saturday morning spent supporting local Fraser Valley agriculture and artisans.
What to Expect
Authentic Local Selection: Adheres to a strict policy ensuring all products are made, baked, or grown by the vendors, offering high-quality produce, honey, and meats.
Handcrafted Artisans: A vibrant collection of local makers selling unique items such as jewelry, woodworking, and natural skincare.
Community Hub: Often features live music and community tents, creating a welcoming social environment for residents and visitors alike.
Seasonal Surprises: Because Mission is in a rich agricultural belt, expect to find excellent seasonal specialties like berries in the summer and hearty squashes in the fall.
Indoors for Winter: While the summer market is in the park, the community keeps the spirit alive with a special indoor Christmas Market in early December.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early May through late October.
Day: Every Saturday, rain or shine.
Hours: 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM.
Location: Centennial Park (7871 Taulbut Street), Mission (South Side of the park on 11th Avenue).
Payment: Most vendors accept cards; the info tent is available to help with market inquiries and token programs.
Pet Policy: Friendly, leashed dogs are welcome to join you as you browse.
Tips
Since the market is in Centennial Park, bring the family and enjoy the playground, picnic areas, or a walk through the trails after you finish shopping.
Mark your calendar for the Christmas Market on Saturday, December 5, 2026, held indoors at the Clarke Theatre for holiday gifts and seasonal treats.
To get the best pick of popular items like fresh-baked bread or early-season berries, aim to arrive right at 10:00 AM.
The market runs rain or shine in the park; wear comfortable shoes suitable for grass and paths.
Look out for special “30 Years” celebrations and limited-edition anniversary events scheduled throughout the 2026 season.

places.name: Haney Farmers’ Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/farmers-market-in-memorial-peace-park-maple-ridge-canada-gm1679100842-536530826

The Haney Farmers’ Market is a quintessential community gathering spot located in the heart of Maple Ridge. Set in the expansive Memorial Peace Park, it offers a scenic and spacious shopping environment that highlights the agricultural abundance of the surrounding Fraser Valley.
What to Expect
Parkside Atmosphere: Held in a beautiful town square setting with plenty of green space, mature trees, and a permanent bandstand for live performances.
Diverse Vendor Mix: Features a wide range of stalls, including conventional and organic farmers, specialty meat producers, and local fishers.
Artisanal and Gourmet Goods: A high-quality selection of kitchen table items such as small-batch hot sauces, artisanal vinegars, local honey, and freshly roasted coffee.
Handmade Crafts: A dedicated section for local artisans selling unique pottery, hand-sewn textiles, jewelry, and woodworking.
Community Events: Frequently hosts themed days, such as Berry Festival or Harvest Day, which include extra activities for children and educational workshops.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early May through late October.
Special Events: Often holds a special season-opener in mid-April (coinciding with Earth Day) and a market on Canada Day (July 1st) if it falls on or near a weekend.
Day: Every Saturday, rain or shine.
Hours: 9:00 AM – 2:00 PM.
Location: Memorial Peace Park (11900 224 Street), Maple Ridge.
Payment: Most vendors are equipped for Debit and Credit; "Market Money" tokens are usually available at the information tent.
Pet Policy: Leashed, well-behaved dogs are welcome to join their owners in the park.
Tips
The market is adjacent to the ACT Arts Centre and the Maple Ridge Public Library, making it easy to combine your grocery shopping with a visit to a gallery or a book pickup.
Ample underground parking is available at the Civic Centre, and there are several free public lots within a two-block radius of the park.
This is a popular neighborhood hub; for the best choice of specialty items like farm eggs or sourdough, aim to arrive in the first hour.
The market often hosts several high-quality food trucks; grab a meal and enjoy it on the grass near the bandstand while listening to local musicians.
In line with local sustainability initiatives, bring your own reusable bags, produce mesh, and egg cartons to help minimize waste.

places.name: Pitt Meadows Farmers Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/onion-harvest-gm1062753904-284121623

The Pitt Meadows Farmers Market is a vibrant community-driven market that celebrates the rich agricultural heritage of the area. Located in the heart of the city, it offers a relaxed, friendly environment where residents and visitors can connect directly with the people who produce their food.
What to Expect
Community Atmosphere: A cozy, welcoming market that serves as a weekly gathering spot for families and neighbors.
Farm-Fresh Selection: Features a curated array of seasonal fruits and vegetables, with a strong emphasis on locally grown berries, corn, and greenhouse produce.
Gourmet & Prepared Foods: High-quality stalls offering artisanal breads, local honey, small-batch preserves, and unique spice blends.
Artisanal Makers: A rotating selection of local crafters selling handmade jewelry, natural body care products, and custom home decor.
Live Local Music: Often features performances by local musicians, providing a pleasant soundtrack for your evening shopping.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early June through late September.
Day: Every Tuesday, rain or shine.
Hours: 3:00 PM – 7:00 PM (Note: Check local signage for the latest seasonal update).
Location: Spirit Square (12027 Harris Road), Pitt Meadows.
Payment: Most vendors accept major credit and debit cards; carrying some cash is helpful for faster transactions at smaller farm stalls.
Pet Policy: Leashed, well-behaved dogs are welcome to accompany you through the market.
Tips
Since the market runs on Tuesday evenings, it’s the ideal time to restock fresh ingredients for the remainder of the week without the weekend rush.
Located right next to the Pitt Meadows Public Library, you can easily pair your grocery run with a family trip for books and media.
Take advantage of the prepared food vendors or nearby local eateries to grab dinner and enjoy it outdoors in the square.
The market is conveniently located near the city’s trail system, making it a perfect destination for those arriving by foot or bicycle.
Check the market's social media pages on Monday evenings for a vendor map and a list of featured food trucks for the following day.

places.name: Port Coquitlam Farmers’ Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/freshly-harvested-organic-pickling-cukes-and-cucumber-at-port-coquitlam-farmers-gm2166548866-586648314

The Port Coquitlam Farmers’ Market is a quintessential community gathering spot that brings a lively, festive energy to the city’s downtown core. Set in the expansive Terry Fox Hometown Square, it serves as a central hub where residents can access the freshest bounty of the Fraser Valley while enjoying local entertainment.
What to Expect
Modern Plaza Setting: Held at the POHO (Port Coquitlam) Community Centre, the market utilizes a sleek, paved outdoor space that is comfortable and easy to navigate.
Direct-from-Farm Produce: A strong emphasis on seasonal BC agriculture, including berries, stone fruits, and greenhouse vegetables sourced from nearby farms.
Handcrafted Boutique Goods: Features a rotating selection of local artisans offering everything from hand-poured candles and natural skincare to custom textiles and jewelry.
Prepared Food & Bakeries: Excellent options for fresh-baked sourdough, artisanal treats, local honey, and small-batch preserves.
Social Atmosphere: With live music and a nearby playground, it’s a popular multi-generational destination where neighbors often stop to chat.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early June through late September.
Day: Every Thursday, rain or shine.
Hours: 3:00 PM – 7:00 PM.
Location: Terry Fox Hometown Square (Port Coquitlam Community Centre), 2150 Wilson Ave.
Payment: Most vendors are equipped for Debit and Credit; "Market Money" tokens can be purchased at the information tent.
Pet Policy: Well-behaved, leashed dogs are welcome to join their owners.
Tips
Because the market runs on Thursday evenings, it’s a perfect stop for those heading home from the nearby West Coast Express station or the Mary Hill Bypass.
The market is located right next to the Port Coquitlam Community Centre, which features a popular spray park and playground for children.
Significant free parking is available in the community centre lot and the surrounding street parking in the downtown core.
Take advantage of the food trucks and prepared meal vendors to pick up a fresh, locally-sourced dinner for a hassle-free Thursday night.
Shoppers are encouraged to bring their own bags and containers to help support the market's commitment to reducing waste.

places.name: Port Moody Summer Farmers Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/organic-produce-farmers-market-gm479474260-68418949

The Port Moody Summer Farmers Market is a vibrant mid-week destination that transforms the recreation grounds into a bustling marketplace. It provides a rare opportunity for local residents to stock up on fresh Fraser Valley produce without having to wait for the weekend rush.
What to Expect
Mid-Week Focus: A smaller, more intimate selection compared to the winter market, prioritizing high-quality seasonal produce and artisanal grab-and-go meals.
Summer Bounty: Strong representation from regional farmers offering peak-season berries, stone fruits, and greenhouse vegetables.
Handmade & Homegrown: Features a curated rotation of bakers, foragers, and local artisans selling unique crafts and apothecary items.
Evening Vibe: Often includes live acoustic music and a selection of food trucks, creating a festive social atmosphere for a Wednesday afternoon out.
Brewery Row Proximity: Many shoppers enjoy a market and a pint routine, visiting the nearby famous craft breweries after finishing their shopping.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early June through mid-October.
Day: Every Wednesday, rain or shine.
Hours: 3:00 PM – 7:00 PM.
Location: Port Moody Recreation Complex (300 Ioco Rd), Port Moody.
Payment: Most vendors are set up for contactless payment (Debit/Credit); cash is helpful for smaller farm stalls.
Pet Policy: Leashed, well-behaved dogs are welcome in the outdoor marketplace.
Tips
Located a short walk from Inlet Centre SkyTrain Station. You can also arrive via the scenic walking trails that lead from the water and Rocky Point Park.
The market gets particularly busy around 5:00 PM; for the best selection of fresh eggs and popular baked goods, try to arrive right at 3:00 PM.
Pick up some fresh snacks and head over to Rocky Point Park or Buntzen Lake (about 20 minutes by car) for a mid-week picnic.
Since it’s at the Rec Complex, it’s easy to pair your visit with a trip to the library or a workout.

places.name: Port Moody Winter Farmers Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/organic-apples-gm810370044-131106557

One of the most established winter resources in the Lower Mainland, the Port Moody Winter Farmers Market provides consistent access to local food throughout the colder months. It serves as a cozy community anchor, keeping the connection between farmers and shoppers alive all year round.
What to Expect
Hearty Seasonal Staples: Focuses on cold-weather crops like root vegetables, hearty greens, and squash, alongside pasture-raised meats and frozen local berries.
Gourmet Pantry Prep: An abundance of small-batch preserves, local honey, artisanal oils, and shelf-stable goods perfect for winter cooking.
Cozy Indoor/Outdoor Hybrid: The market utilizes both the courtyard and indoor space of the Recreation Complex to keep shoppers comfortable regardless of the rain or snow.
Artisanal Gifts: A top destination during November and December for unique, handcrafted holiday gifts and seasonal decor.
Prepared Comfort Foods: Expect local vendors selling frozen ramen, soups, stews, and fresh-baked pies to get you through the week.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from early November through late April.
Day: Every Sunday (typically excluding the last Sunday of December and the first Sunday of January).
Hours: 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM.
Location: Port Moody Recreation Complex (300 Ioco Rd), Port Moody.
Payment: Most vendors accept cards; "Market Money" tokens can be purchased at the information tent for use at cash-only stalls.
Pet Policy: Leashed dogs are permitted in the outdoor market areas.
Tips
Even with the indoor/outdoor setup, warm layers and waterproof shoes are recommended to navigate the full range of vendors comfortably.
In late autumn, the market takes on a festive holiday atmosphere; it’s an excellent alternative to busy malls for unique gifts.
Winter attendance can shift due to weather or seasonal harvests; follow their social media on Saturday evening to see which specific vendors will be on-site.
Newport Village is just a few steps away, offering several excellent cafes where you can grab a hot chocolate or coffee after your winter shop.

places.name: Surrey Urban Farmers’ Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/organic-raspberries-and-blueberries-in-sustainable-compostable-and-recyclable-gm2166548919-586648339

The Surrey Urban Farmers’ Market is a multicultural, non-profit hub that serves as a vital link between local growers and the diverse North Surrey community. Now located in the expansive Royal Kwantlen Park, it offers a high-energy, inclusive environment where food security and community connection are the top priorities.
What to Expect
Multicultural Bounty: Reflecting Surrey’s diverse population, you’ll find a wide range of international prepared foods alongside traditional Fraser Valley produce.
Lively Community Spirit: Features vibrant live music performances, community workshops, and a rotating list of local artisans and crafters.
Parkside Location: Set in a large park with tennis courts, a skate park, a playground, and an outdoor pool, making it a perfect anchor for a full family day out.
Inclusive Programming: Host to initiatives like the Power of Produce (PoP) Kids Club and the Farmers’ Market Nutrition Coupon Program, ensuring fresh food is accessible to all.
Make It, Bake It, Grow It: Every vendor is an authentic local producer, ensuring that your spending stays within the regional economy.
Key Information
Season: Open annually from early June through early October.
Day: Every Saturday, rain or shine.
Hours: 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM.
Location: Royal Kwantlen Park (at the corner of 104th Avenue & Old Yale Road), Surrey.
Payment: Most vendors accept credit and debit cards; tokens are available at the market info tent for use at cash-only stalls.
Pet Policy: Well-behaved, leashed dogs are welcome.
Tips
The market is a short walk from the Surrey Central SkyTrain Station and sits on major bus routes, making it one of the most accessible markets in the city.
The early bird regulars typically arrive right at 10:00 AM to secure the best farm-fresh eggs and popular baked goods.
Bring your swimsuit or tennis racket! Since the market is in Royal Kwantlen Park, you can enjoy the outdoor pool or courts after you finish your grocery shopping.
There is a dedicated parking area in Royal Kwantlen Park for market visitors, though it can fill up quickly on sunny days.
This is a smaller, community-focused market, so take the time to ask farmers about their crops—many are happy to share tips on how to prepare unique seasonal vegetables.

places.name: The Clayton Community Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/bunch-of-fresh-radishes-gm2166060404-586199123

The Clayton Community Market is a relationship-driven bi-weekly market designed to foster neighbors supporting neighbors. Located in the parking lot of the modern Clayton Community Centre, it is widely loved for its family-friendly atmosphere and its focus on local growers and creators.
What to Expect
Family Fun Zone: A dedicated space for children to play, making it a popular choice for parents looking for a relaxed weekend outing.
Curated Vendor Mix: Host to over 65 vendors, ranging from fresh local produce and farm-fresh eggs to unique artisan crafts and jewelry.
Handmade Gourmet Goods: Features a strong selection of Make, Bake, Grow items like artisanal jams, fresh-baked breads, and authentic prepared foods.
Social & Community Vibe: Known for its friendly energy where regular shoppers often recognize and catch up with their favorite local makers.
Accessible Layout: The market is set on a paved surface with modern paths, making it very accessible for strollers and mobility aids.
Key Information
Season: Runs annually from May through October.
Day: Bi-weekly Sundays (every other week); the market typically skips long weekends.
Hours: 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM.
Location: Clayton Community Centre (7155 187A Street), Surrey.
Payment: Most vendors are equipped for card payments; "Market Dollars" are often available at the information booth for use throughout the market.
Pet Policy: Leashed, friendly dogs are welcome in the outdoor market area.
Tips for Success
Because the market runs bi-weekly, it is always a good idea to confirm it by checking the market's social media or website before heading out.
Since it’s located at the Community Centre, you can pair your market trip with the library or other indoor facilities.
If you live nearby, walking or biking to the center is recommended as the parking lot can get busy during peak market hours.
The Family Fun Zone is a major highlight; look for special activities or themes during the summer months.
Take advantage of the high-quality control standards to try unique items you won't find in traditional grocery stores, such as specialty preserves or locally crafted soaps.

places.name: Ambleside Farmers’ Market
body: https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/organic-fresh-berries-gm2122753326-567592120

The Ambleside Farmers’ Market is a premier West Vancouver destination that combines a sophisticated shopping experience with a stunning coastal backdrop. Located at the entrance to Ambleside Park, it serves as a weekly social hub for North Shore residents looking for high-quality BC produce and artisanal goods.
What to Expect
Upscale Artisan Selection: Known for its high concentration of professional makers selling gourmet pantry staples, high-end jewelry, and West Coast-inspired art.
Regional Agricultural Bounty: Features a diverse array of vendors from the Sea-to-Sky corridor and the Fraser Valley, offering organic fruits, vegetables, and farm-fresh eggs.
